Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

# Quizzy Architecture Notes (Release 1: Moderator Prep)

## Stack & Serving
- Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4.1, SQLite3 (all database files stored under `storage/`).
- Propshaft + Importmap + Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus); no Node.js build step.
- `bin/serve` prepares the SQLite database (`db:prepare`), compiles assets (`assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in production mode on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (no SSL redirect, accepts all host names).

## Moderator Area (`/moderate`)
- Protected by HTTP Basic authentication in `Moderate::BaseController` using constant-time `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- Models:
  - `Quiz` (`title` required) has many `questions` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Question` (`body` required, `position`, `active` default `true`) has many `options` ordered by `position, id`.
  - `Option` (`body` required, `correct` default `false`, `position`).
- Question option validation runs on submitted form rows (`Question#option_rows`) inside a transaction:
  - Blank option rows are skipped.
  - Requires at least 2 non-empty options (`"Add at least two options"`) and at least 1 correct option (`"Mark at least one option as correct"`).
  - On validation failure, no DB writes occur and all submitted rows (including blanks, newly added rows, and checkboxes) are preserved in the re-rendered form.
- Dynamic option rows are handled by `app/javascript/controllers/option_rows_controller.js`.
- Active toggle on the quiz page submits immediately via `this.form.requestSubmit()`.

## Preview Mode (`/moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/preview`)
- Plays active questions in order (`quiz.active_questions`).
- Preview state (`step`, `score`, `picked_id`, `finished`) is passed via a signed token (`Rails.application.message_verifier(:quizzy_preview)`) in query/form parameters so no preview answers are stored in the database or session.

## Quiz Export & Import
- **Export** (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export`, linked as `"Export"` on the quiz page):
  - `Quiz#export_payload` builds `{ title, questions: [{ text, active, options: [{ text, correct }] }] }` ordered by `position, id` with no extra keys.
  - Rendered via `JSON.pretty_generate` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
- **Import** (`GET/POST /moderate/quizzes/import`, opened via `"Import quiz"` button on `/moderate`):
  - `QuizImport` validates JSON syntax, structure, non-blank title/question/option texts, boolean types for optional `active` (defaults to `true`) and `correct` (defaults to `false`), at least 2 options per question, and at least 1 correct option per question.
  - All database writes run inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction`, ensuring invalid payloads create nothing (neither quiz nor partial questions).
  - Successful import always creates a new `Quiz` (even if a quiz with the same title exists) and redirects to its moderator page.

class Question < ApplicationRecord

  DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create
  after_destroy :renumber_quiz_questions

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: :option_rows_submitted?

  def option_rows
    @option_rows ||= if persisted? && options.any?
      options.map { |opt| OptionRow.new(body: opt.body, correct: opt.correct?) }
    else
      Array.new(DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS) { OptionRow.new(body: "", correct: false) }
    end
  end

  def assign_option_rows(raw_rows)
    @option_rows_submitted = true
    rows = case raw_rows
    when ActionController::Parameters
      raw_rows.to_unsafe_h
    when Hash
      raw_rows
    else
      {}
    end

    bool = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new
    @option_rows = rows
      .sort_by { |key, _| key.to_i }
      .map do |_, attrs|
        attrs = attrs.respond_to?(:to_h) ? attrs.to_h : {}
        OptionRow.new(
          body: attrs["body"].to_s,
          correct: bool.cast(attrs["correct"]) == true
        )
      end
  end

  def save_with_options!
    return false unless valid?

    transaction do
      save!
      if option_rows_submitted?
        options.destroy_all
        non_empty_option_rows.each_with_index do |row, idx|
          options.create!(
            body: row.body.strip,
            correct: row.correct,
            position: idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    false
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def option_rows_submitted?
    @option_rows_submitted == true
  end

  def non_empty_option_rows
    option_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    non_empty = non_empty_option_rows
    if non_empty.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif non_empty.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end
  end

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?
    return unless quiz

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by(delta)
    quiz.with_lock do
      ordered = quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return if idx.nil?

      target_idx = idx + delta
      return if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_columns(position: new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  def renumber_quiz_questions
    return unless quiz

    quiz.questions.order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, i|
      new_pos = i + 1
      question.update_columns(position: new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
    end
  end

**Comprehensive Quiz Game Architecture**

Okay, so I've got this game architecture to design, and it looks like a fun challenge. First, I'm allowing the same origin for HTTP, so I can seamlessly handle different hostnames, which is a good starting point. Now, let's nail down the core components: the database models, the broadcast strategy (crucial!), the routes, controllers, views, and JavaScript interactions.

### Data Model Design

The database needs to be super clean and scalable. I'm thinking:

*   **`Game`**: The central table. It links to a `Quiz` (and I need to handle quiz deletion cleanly with `dependent: :destroy`), and stores game-specific data: the game code, snapshot of quiz title, current status (lobby, question open, etc.), index for current question, a version number for optimistic locking, start/end timestamps. I'm using an enum for `status` with values "lobby", "question\_open", "question\_closed", and "finished". The `version` increment is key – it's atomic and helps clients know if they've missed an update.

*   **`GameQuestion`**: These are question snapshots, associated with a specific `Game`. These are snapshots so that editing quiz questions later won't break the game. Each game has a set of `game\_questions`, ordered by position.

*   **`GameOption`**: Question options, linked to `GameQuestion`. Each has a body, a boolean 'correct' flag, and position.

*   **`Player`**: Stores player information for a `Game` including their name and a unique token. There's a join index for `game\_id` and `created\_at` to optimize queries for showing joined players.

*   **`Answer`**: Tracks player responses. It has unique index on `(player, game_question)`. This is super clean – changing an answer is just an update to a single row. Counting answers is super easy with the unique index.

I'm also doing a quick check on SQLite concurrency because we're talking about dozens, or even a couple of hundred phones simultaneously tapping options. I'll make sure the database `timeout` is long enough and SQLite is in WAL mode, which is the default in Rails 8. I'll need to keep transactions short (no broadcasts inside DB transactions) to avoid lock contention.

### Broadcast & Security Architecture

Now for the security-critical part: broadcasting. My rule is that players cannot know the correct answer before the question is closed. I need separate broadcasts for the moderator's screen (`/moderate/games/:id`) and the players (`/play/:code`).

*   **Moderator Big Screen**: This is protected by HTTP Basic Auth. I'm using a signed stream name generated by `Rails.application.message_verifier(:turbo_streams)`. I'll broadcast updates to a specific `turbo_stream_from` (like `[@game, :moderator]`) on `#big_screen`, keeping it separate from the public stream.

*   **Player Public Game Stream**: This is for the players and goes to the `/play/:code` route. This is where I need to be extra careful:
    *   **Question open**: Broadcast the same question text and options to all players (no correctness information!).
    *   **Question closed**: I NEED to send personalized feedback ("Correct!", "Wrong!", "No answer") to each player. This means I can't just have one broadcast that contains both a shared view AND the personalized bits.

I'm evaluating two approaches for broadcasts, and the hybrid approach seems the best:

*   **Per-player Turbo Stream**: I can use `turbo_stream_from @game, @player` for each player, so each one gets their personalized updates. Rendering many partials in a loop can be slow, but it's super clean and doesn't leak info. We're thinking that with 50-500 players, it's pretty fast (5-50ms). Each player is just getting THEIR exact personalized HTML. This is looking very, very clean.
    *   When the moderator clicks "Finish" (or any button), it will broadcast out to the `#@game, @player`.
*   **Shared broadcast + personalized updates**: The second idea is to send a shared broadcast to `[@game, :players]`. On 'question\_open' and 'finished' state, the shared broadcast works well and updates all phones very fast. When a question closes, the players NEED personalized feedback, so I'm thinking a tiny Turbo Stream to the shared broadcast would tell the player to fetch the `/play/:code/state` API endpoint. I'm thinking this will be fast enough, and would reuse existing code for Wi-Fi reconnect recovery

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed finished].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :quiz_title, presence: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(
        quiz: quiz,
        quiz_title: quiz.title,
        code: generate_unique_code,
        status: "lobby",
        current_question_index: 0,
        version: 1
      )

      quiz.active_questions.includes(:options).order(:position, :id).each_with_index do |question, q_idx|
        gq = game.game_questions.create!(
          body: question.body,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )

        question.options.sort_by { |o| [ o.position, o.id ] }.each_with_index do |option, o_idx|
          gq.game_options.create!(
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET.sample }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def finished?
    status == "finished"
  end

  def ordered_questions
    game_questions.includes(:game_options).order(:position, :id).to_a
  end

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if lobby? || finished?

    ordered_questions[current_question_index]
  end

  def last_question?
    total = total_questions
    total.zero? || current_question_index >= total - 1
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_question
    return 0 unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).count
  end

  def option_answer_counts(question = current_question)
    return {} unless question

    answers.where(game_question_id: question.id).group(:game_option_id).count
  end

  def moderator_state_key
    "m-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}"
  end

  def player_state_key(player, answer = nil)
    if player.nil?
      "u-#{finished? ? "finished" : "join"}"
    else
      "p-#{status}-q#{current_question_index}-v#{version}-a#{answer&.game_option_id}"
    end
  end

  def start!
    with_lock do
      return false unless lobby?

      if game_questions.empty?
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          started_at: Time.current,
          finished_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: 0,
          started_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def finish_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_open?

      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def next_question!
    with_lock do
      return false unless question_closed?

      next_idx = current_question_index + 1
      if next_idx < game_questions.count
        update!(
          status: "question_open",
          current_question_index: next_idx,
          version: version + 1
        )
      else
        update!(
          status: "finished",
          finished_at: Time.current,
          version: version + 1
        )
      end
      true
    end
  end

  def end_game!
    with_lock do
      return false if finished?

      update!(
        status: "finished",
        finished_at: Time.current,
        version: version + 1
      )
      true
    end
  end

  def join_player!(name)
    trimmed = name.to_s.strip
    return nil if trimmed.blank?

    with_lock do
      return :finished if finished?

      player = players.create!(name: trimmed)
      update!(version: version + 1)
      player
    end
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    return :closed if player.nil?

    with_lock do
      return :closed unless question_open?

      question = current_question
      return :closed unless question && question.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return :invalid unless option

      answer = answers.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
      if answer.game_option_id != option.id
        answer.game_option = option
        answer.save!
        update!(version: version + 1)
      end
      answer
    end
  end

class GameBroadcaster
  class << self
    def broadcast_moderator_stage(game, join_url: nil)
      game = game.reload
      stage_html = render_html("moderate/games/stage", game: game, join_url: join_url)
      marker_html = render_html("moderate/games/state_marker", game: game)

      stream = turbo_stream_replace("big_screen_stage", stage_html) +
               turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)

      Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
    end

    def broadcast_moderator_counters(game)
      game = game.reload
      marker_html = render_html("moderate/games/state_marker", game: game)

      if game.lobby?
        counter_html = render_html("moderate/games/lobby_players_count", game: game)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("lobby_players_count", counter_html) +
                 turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
      elsif game.question_open? || game.question_closed?
        counter_html = render_html("moderate/games/question_answers_counter", game: game)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("question_answers_counter", counter_html) +
                 turbo_stream_replace("moderator_state_marker", marker_html)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :moderator ], content: stream)
      end
    end

    def broadcast_players_stage(game)
      game = game.reload

      case game.status
      when "question_open"
        stage_html = render_html("play/stage", game: game, player: true, player_answer: nil)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
        game.players.find_each do |player|
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end
      when "question_closed"
        current_q = game.current_question
        answers_by_player_id = if current_q
          game.answers.where(game_question_id: current_q.id).includes(:game_option).index_by(&:player_id)
        else
          {}
        end

        game.players.find_each do |player|
          stage_html = render_html(
            "play/stage",
            game: game,
            player: player,
            player_answer: answers_by_player_id[player.id]
          )
          stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end
      when "finished"
        stage_html = render_html("play/stage", game: game, player: true, player_answer: nil)
        stream = turbo_stream_replace("player_stage", stage_html)
        game.players.find_each do |player|
          Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, player ], content: stream)
        end
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to([ game, :join ], content: stream)
      end
    end

    private

    def render_html(partial, locals)
      ApplicationController.renderer.render(
        partial: partial,
        formats: [ :html ],
        locals: locals
      )
    end

    def turbo_stream_replace(target, html)
      %(<turbo-stream action="replace" target="#{target}"><template>#{html}</template></turbo-stream>\n)
    end
  end
end
EOF

    @player = result
    cookies.signed[player_cookie_key(@game)] = {
      value: @player.token,

      same_site: :lax

messages.thinking: **A Deep Dive into a Nasty CSS Flexbox Bug and a Robust Fix** Whoa, that was a close one! Our system tests just snagged a doozy of a bug! I'm looking at this error message: `expected to find text "Players: 0" in "...\nPlayers:\n0\n...". (However, it was found 1 time including non-visible text.)` - seriously, why did we have that newline show up in the text content? Aha! It's that `.counter-pill` element in `quizzy.css` with `display: inline-flex`. It turns out that when a flex container has an anonymous text node like "Players: " right next to a `0` element, Chromium's `innerText` decides to treat them as block-level boxes separated by newlines, leading to `"Players:\n0"` instead of what we expect: "Players: 0". Thank goodness we were testing this in Chromium! If our QA tests were doing `assert_text "Players: 0"` or `assert_text "Players: 2"`, they would have *failed* on this! The fix is thankfully straightforward: wrap the "Players: " and the dynamic count within a single `Players: <%= game.players_count %>`. That forces everything into a single inline text element. Now, `innerText` will be the single line "Players: 0" we need, while preserving the visual styling! Okay, time to be thorough. Let's scan the codebase for *any* other instances of `display: flex` or `display: grid` that are splitting text nodes, and prevent a repeat. 1. `_lobby_players_count.html.erb`: The fix is exactly the same: `Players: <%= game.players_count %>` 2. `_question_answers_counter.html.erb`: This is safe. It's not a flex element, just plain text "Answers: 1 / 2". 3. `stage-option`: This is *also* safe. It's `display: flex`, but each label ("Correct", "1", the option title) is in its own ``, so it's a clean match. 4. `play-option`: This is safe, too. The labels are nicely contained within their own spans. Alright, I'm going to implement the fix for `_lobby_players_count.html.erb` immediately, and then we'll re-run those system tests to be 100% sure we've squashed this bug for good!

cat <<'EOF' >> docs/architecture.md

## Live Game (Release 2)
- **Models**:
  - `Game` (`quiz_id`, unique 5-char `code`, `quiz_title` snapshot, `status`: `lobby | question_open | question_closed | finished`, `current_question_index`, monotonically increasing `version`).
  - `GameQuestion` & `GameOption`: snapshots of the quiz's active questions and their options created when starting a game (`Game.create_from_quiz!`), so inactive questions are skipped and later edits/deletes on the quiz never affect running or past games.
  - `Player` (`game_id`, `name`, unique `token`): stored in an HTTP-only signed cookie scoped per game (`cookies.signed["quizzy_player_#{game.id}"]`) so the same browser remembers the player within a game while remaining completely independent across multiple games of the same quiz.
  - `Answer` (`game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`): unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]` ensures changing an answer updates the single row in place (`last pick counts`).
- **Moderator Big Screen (`/moderate/games/:id`)**:
  - Protected by `Moderate::BaseController` HTTP Basic Auth; uses full-bleed `layouts/screen.html.erb`.
  - Lobby displays quiz title, plain-text join URL, inline SVG QR code (`rqrcode`), live `"Players: N"` counter, and `"Start"` button.
  - Open question shows `"Question X of Y"`, options, live `"Answers: A / P"` counter, and `"Finish"` button.
  - Closed question shows per-option counts, `"Correct"` badges on correct options, and `"Next"` (or `"End quiz"` on the last question).
  - Finished state shows `"The quiz is over"`.
- **Player Experience (`/play/:code`)**:
  - Public routes under `PlayController` (no moderator auth).
  - Players can join at any time before `finished`; once `finished`, `/play/:code` shows `"The quiz is over"` and refuses new joins.
  - While `question_open`, player templates and broadcasts never reference `option.correct?` so correctness cannot leak in page source or WebSocket payloads.
  - After `"Finish"`, each player receives their personalized outcome (`"Correct!"`, `"Wrong!"`, or `"No answer"`).
- **Live Updates & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience**:
  - Separate signed Turbo Stream channels: `[game, :moderator]` (big screen), `[game, player]` (each joined player), and `[game, :join]` (unjoined join screen for game-end transitions).
  - `app/javascript/controllers/live_game_controller.js` observes `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` connection state, `visibilitychange`, and `online` events, syncing missed state transitions via `state` endpoints (`?v=<state_key>`, returning `204 No Content` when up to date) and falling back to 2-second polling only while the WebSocket is disconnected.
EOF
